summary: A candidate and his wife name the real worry as whether he can still be present for young children.
realLife: In late 2006 Barack Obama told an elder adviser that he and Michelle were most concerned about whether he could be a good father. The adviser said that if he ran he should do it while the children were young, because a parent matters most in the teen years. Obama said he would pass that on to Michelle, who by a close friend's account wanted a present father and expected the race to be hard.
gates: The player has a child at home.
The player is weighing a larger race than their current office.
weights: How much the spouse already carries at home.
inGame: A young child at home and a spouse in the household can carry it, with the family-filing scene as the venue.

turns.what: The spouse says the timing is wrong and asks him to wait until the children are older.
turns.pulledBy: Very young children, a spouse already stretched.
turns.writesBack: The filing is delayed or the tie to the spouse strains.

turns.what: They agree it will be hard, make a list of what must stay protected, and go ahead.
turns.writesBack: A shared commitment recorded on the household.

turns.what: He decides the right time has passed and does not run.
turns.pulledBy: Teen children, a spouse's lingering doubt.
turns.writesBack: No filing; a missed-chance memory on the player.
